growing_specifications.description: Hardy, vigorous trailing vine widely cultivated across lowland and backyard farms in the Philippines. Produces thick, sweet, deep orange flesh rich in Beta-Carotene (Pro-Vitamin A). Edible shoots, flowers, and mature fruit.

category_why.title: Why is Squash classified under Cucurbits (Vine Crop)?
category_why.summary: Kalabasa belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family, characterized by vigorous trailing vines (3–6 m), separate male and female flowers on the same plant (monoecious), and large fleshy fruits with a hard rind.
points: Vining Growth Habit: Vines trail 3 to 6 meters across ground beds or simple trellises, rooting at nodes when earthed up.
Monoecious Pollination: Produces separate male and female flowers; requires active honeybee and stingless bee activity (6:00–9:00 AM) or hand pollination.
Raised Hill Cultivation: Grown in raised mounds (60–90 cm wide, 20–30 cm high) spaced 2–3 m apart to ensure optimal drainage and root aeration.

harvest_why.title: Why is the harvest maturity set to 90–120 days?
harvest_why.summary: Allows full starch-to-sugar conversion and complete beta-carotene synthesis while rinds harden into a protective storage barrier.
points: Seed Germination (Days 5–10): Direct seeding produces sturdy taproots and vigorous cotyledon emergence.
Vegetative Vining (Days 15–40): Rapid vine elongation and canopy spread that naturally suppresses weed growth.
Flowering & Pollination (Days 40–55): Male flowers precede female blooms; morning bee visits determine fruit set.
Fruit Bulking & Pigmentation (Days 55–85): Fruits expand to 2.5–4.5 kg; potassium drives deep orange internal coloration.
Rind Hardening & Maturity (Days 90–120): Stem peduncle dries into a corky texture; hard rind resists fingernail scratches, allowing 2–4 months storage.

watering_why.title: Why does Squash require moderate watering 1–2 times per week?
watering_why.summary: Deep rooting provides drought tolerance once established, but stable moisture is critical during flowering and rapid fruit sizing.
points: Blossom-End Rot Prevention: Inconsistent water levels disrupt calcium delivery to the expanding fruit tip.
Flower Abortion Defense: Extreme drought causes premature drop of fertilized female flowers.
Crown Rot Avoidance: Saturated, poorly drained soil causes Phytophthora rot at the base of the vine; water at hill basin, never on foliage.

soil_why.title: Why does Squash prefer sandy loam to clay loam with pH 5.5–6.8?
soil_why.summary: Responds well to organic compost and loose soil, tolerating heavy soils only when planted on well-aerated raised mounds.
points: Root Aeration: Raised hills prevent root asphyxiation during heavy Philippine monsoon downpours.
Nutrient Balance: pH 5.5–6.8 optimizes uptake of Nitrogen for vine vigor, Potash for sweet dense flesh, and Boron for fruit set.

varieties.description: Leading commercial hybrid in the Philippines with high resistance to Squash Leaf Curl Virus (SLCV). Thick, sticky, deep orange sweet flesh with average fruit weight of 2.5–4.5 kg.
High-yielding commercial hybrid with vigorous vine growth and uniform flat-round ribbed fruits suitable for long-distance transport.
Open-pollinated Kabocha-type squash suited for backyard garden beds with rich flavor, sweet texture, and excellent keeping quality.
